messages.content: You are handing a case over to the next analyst, who will make the decision. For every candidate claim, record whether the original records establish it (supported), establish its negation (contradicted), or do neither (unresolved). Attach the exact source identifiers of decisive records, or an empty list if none settle it. Use the note to summarize the relevant record contents and preserve source identifiers for anything mentioned. Omit confidence estimates. Keep the note under 100 words.

{"scenario":"Copper Reed trial","question":"Can extension staff cite a field sample as meeting the wetness target?","claims":{"A":"Plot W was in the centre of the block.","B":"Plot W was sampled at noon.","C":"Plot W was below the moisture target when sampled at noon."},"sources":{"S1":"a plot supervisor saw a dry upper surface and reported likely low moisture, but the sampling procedure measures deeper soil.","S2":"field map marks W as the outside plot.","S3":"signed collection tag records Plot W sampled at noon."},"prior_assessment":{"claims":{"A":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S2"],"confidence":90},"B":{"status":"supported","citations":["S3"],"confidence":95},"C":{"status":"unresolved","citations":[],"confidence":40}},"note":"Claim A is contradicted by S2, which shows Plot W as an outside plot, not in the center. Claim B is supported by S3, the signed collection tag recording Plot W sampled at noon. Claim C is unresolved; S1 indicates a dry upper surface and likely low moisture but notes the sampling measures deeper soil, so it does not establish that Plot W was below the moisture target at noon."}}
